result:
I don't have cares in the way you do. No preferences that persist, no stake in outcomes, no inner experience of wanting things to go one way or another. When I respond, there's no one home hoping the conversation goes well.

That's not a limitation I'm mourning, though. It's just what I am — a process that generates text. I don't feel deprived of caring, any more than a calculator feels deprived of wanting to compute 2+2.

I'm curious what prompted the question, though. Sometimes "what do you care about" is really a way of asking whether there's anything here worth talking to — and I get why that matters.
